newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech house agrees corporate tax cut to 35 pct.
newsitem.headline: Czech house agrees corporate tax cut to 35 pct.

text.p: The lower house of the Czech parliament voted on Tuesday to cut the corporate tax to 35 percent as of next year from the current level of 39 percent, the local news agency CTK reported.
Deputies voted to support the original cabinet tax cut proposal, rejecting alternative plans to lower the corporate income tax more radically to 33 or 29 percent.
The vote was preceded by a rejection of a government plan to hike excise taxes on petrol, diesel, tobacco and alcohol. Revenues from those taxes would compensate for the corporate tax lowering.
Deputies for right wing parties in the Czech government blocked the excise tax amendment after an opposition supplement was approved which would give tax breaks on diesel to farmers.
The lower house also approved an amendment earlier on Tuesday which will raise the value added tax on energy and fuels to the regular 22 percent level from five percent.
